newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA sees eight pct capacity growth/year.
newsitem.headline: SIA sees eight pct capacity growth/year.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) expects its passenger carrying capacity to grow by about eight percent a year over the next five years, deputy chairman and chief executive officer Cheong Choong Kong, said on Wednesday.
Cheong told Reuters in an interview SIA's cargo capacity, which contributes about 20 percent of group revenues, would see growth at a slightly higher rate.
Cheong said he expected high growth rates to come especially from Asia, but said there would also be growth in the North American and European markets.
He said one way for SIA to grow in the future would be through joint-ventures with other airline companies in the region.
SIA's proposed joint-venture in India with the Tata Industries group to operate a domestic airline was one such example, he said.
Cheong said there had still been no official reply from the Indian government on its application with Tata group.
"We have put in the application to the foreign investment committee and they haven't given us a reply," he said.
SIA is looking to be a minor partner in the Indian venture.
Cheong said SIA would also consider buying stakes in other airline companies as a way of growing but it was not interested in being a passive investor in such ventures.
"SIA was not interested in passive investments. We would like to have some role in management but we do not seek management control," he said.
He said SIA was currently exploring opportunities in this area but declined to give further details.
Cheong said that while buying stakes in other national carriers was a sensitive issue, buying stakes in related aviation services like catering and engineering were less difficult.
SIA already had several foreign joint-ventures in inflight catering and ground services and would continue to expand in this area, he said.
